subject: Post-call: API/SDK & model fallback policy clarifications for Telos Health
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@teloshealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@teloshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + integration questions (SDK/auth/region/fallbacks)

Hi Samir / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a short list of follow-ups so we can scope the technical deep-dive: 

Recap: 
- Goal: embed Redwood-powered clinical search + structured results into Telos Provider Portal (priority: diagnosis-assist & billing-code suggestions).
- Desired SLOs: P50 latency ~200ms for short queries, P95 under 600ms for interactive use.
- Data residency: US-only (must stay in US regions).

Technical follow-ups we need answers on before the SE deep-dive: 
1) SDK + runtime: preferred client languages (Node/Python/Go)? Any existing infra constraints for adding our SDKs behind a proxy?
2) Auth & secrets: would you prefer API keys with KMS-backed rotation, or OIDC mTLS? Any corporate KMS we must integrate with?
3) Routing & fallback policy: are you OK with an automated fallback chain (higher-cost model -> quantized open model) when latency/capacity pressure occurs, or do you require strict pinned models?
4) Structured output / tool calling: will the billing-code step need FHIR-parsable output or a proprietary JSON schema?
5) Embeddings & re-ranker: estimated index size (docs/patients) and QPS for semantic search?

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-sdk.md (SDK quickstart) and integration-questions.xlsx (short form to capture the answers above).

Next steps: if you can reply to questions 1–5 this week, we’ll schedule a 60-min SE deep-dive (Vivek) and bring a routing/ops proposal + cost ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@teloshealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@teloshealth.com>, procurement@teloshealth.com
Date: 2027-08-31T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + integration questions (SDK/auth/region/fallbacks)

Naomi — thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline: 

1) SDK: primary stack is Node (backend) + React frontend. We’d prefer a thin server-side integration; client-side SDKs not allowed for PHI.
2) Auth: Procurement/security prefers API keys rotated via our AWS KMS. We can support a short-lived token flow if needed, but turnkey API-key + inbound allowlist is easiest for pilot.
3) Fallbacks: We want an explicit fallback chain — allowed to fallback to an open, quantized model for non-PHI queries only. For PHI paths we need strict pinned model(s) and logging.
4) Structured output: Billing-code outputs must map to our internal JSON schema (I attached a sample in a follow-up to Priya). FHIR not required for this phase.
5) Embeddings: initial index ~800k documents, expected QPS ~35 at peak.

Procurement loop: procurement@teloshealth.com is on cc — procurement is requesting an estimated TCO for a 6-month pilot (Hosted vs Dedicated) and a copy of any SLA exceptions for model fallbacks.

Appreciate the next-step calendar invite for the SE deep-dive.

—Samir
Director, Platform Engineering
Telos Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@teloshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-31T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + integration questions (SDK/auth/region/fallbacks)

Samir — great, thanks for the details and for looping procurement in. Quick notes and owners: 

- SDK stack (Node backend) — Ben will own a short integration checklist and a sample Node wrapper to place behind your proxy (Ben will follow up with a repo + code sample).
- Auth (API key + AWS KMS rotation) — Vivek: can you outline options for short-lived tokens versus KMS-provisioned keys and a recommended plan for pilot?
- Fallbacks & PHI: noted that PHI paths must be pinned/strict. We’ll propose a hybrid routing policy that routes PHI-tagged requests only to pinned Dedicated instances (or Hosted with customer-managed VPC), and non-PHI queries can use automated fallback chains.
- Structured output mapping: Naomi to collect sample JSON from Priya before the SE call.
- Embeddings: scale/look: Vivek to propose batch-embedding ingest and candidate re-ranker architecture for ~800k docs.

Proposed SE deep-dive: Tue Sep 7 10:00–11:00 PT. Vivek — can you confirm? I’ll send the invite once we confirm.

Thanks —
Naomi
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@teloshealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@teloshealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T14:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + integration questions (SDK/auth/region/fallbacks)

Hi all — thanks Naomi. Quick technical proposal ahead of the deep-dive so we can be efficient: 

1) Auth & secrets: implement API-key issuance with short-lived edge tokens. Backend flow: Telos requests API key via our onboarding, keys stored in AWS KMS; workload authenticates to Redwood with short-lived tokens minted by a Redwood auth edge that validates KMS ownership. For higher security, we can enable mTLS between your VPC proxy and our ingress.

2) Region routing & PHI isolation: deploy a customer VPC connector in us-east-1. Routing policy: requests tagged as PHI -> route to Dedicated capacity (pinned model host in the US), non-PHI -> route to Hosted pool with fallback chain. We will enforce a header-based tag and provide an SDK helper that sets the tag from your backend logic.

3) Fallback chain (recommended): primary: rwd-gpt-4o (latency ~120–220ms P50), fallback-1: rwd-llm-compact (quantized, faster cost-efficient), fallback-2: community-mosaic-q4 (8-bit) for very high-load/low-cost scenarios. For PHI-tagged calls we will disable fallback beyond a pinned subset you approve. We’ll include cost estimates for each leg in the routing policy UI.

4) Structured output / tool calling: propose using Redwood’s structured tool-calling with a strict JSON schema. We’ll create a mapping adapter for Telos’s billing JSON sample (Priya — please attach) so the LLM emits directly to your schema. For auditability we’ll persist both raw LLM output and normalized JSON.

5) Embeddings & re-ranker: batch ingest via our embeddings pipeline with incremental updates. For 800k documents, recommend a two-tier re-ranker: (a) dense-retriever embedding match, (b) lightweight cross-encoder reranker for top-50 candidates. We’ll size the embedding cluster to meet your QPS target (~35) with autoscale headroom.

Attachments: redwood-routing-proposal-v1.pdf (contains a diagram of the routing policy and fallback cost matrix).

I’ll bring rough cost delta Hosted vs Dedicated to the deep-dive; Naomi / Ben will follow with a Hosted pilot quote and Dedicated sizing options.

Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@teloshealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@teloshealth.com>, procurement@teloshealth.com
Date: 2027-09-02T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + integration questions (SDK/auth/region/fallbacks)

Thanks Vivek / Naomi — proposal sounds reasonable. A few procurement asks before we lock the deep-dive: 

1) Can you send a 6-month cost ballpark for Hosted pilot vs Dedicated pilot (include estimated token costs, reserved capacity delta, and any add-on for SSO/KMS integration)?
2) Any SLA exceptions we’d need to accept for fallback behavior (i.e., if fallback to community models is used during an incident)? Procurement is sensitive to having explicit fallback clauses.
3) Contract timeline: we’d like legal to see a draft SOW by Sep 10 to keep an Oct pilot start.

If you can provide 1–3 this week, we’ll confirm Tue Sep 7 for the technical deep-dive.

—Samir
